captures.text: Humidity study protocol: quantify Lark baseline drift from 30% to 80% relative humidity. The dry control and wet runs are phases of this one study.
Separate Lark experiment approved: battery hours at three radio duty cycles. This has its own outcome and report, independent of the humidity study.
Bench photo description: Lark sensor in humidity chamber beside a dry-control enclosure, both labeled DRIFT. Cable gland looks loose.
Run B dropped after six hours.
The balcony chair's rear rail split along the old screw hole. Clamp a new hardwood insert before reseating the screw.
Lark equipment booking: humidity-drift chamber run Monday; independent battery-duty-cycle run Thursday. The sensor is shared, so reset its firmware between jobs.
DRIFT chamber log clip: humidity ramps smoothly after tightening the cable gland. Dry-control signal remains level through the same interval.
For my 'Run B dropped' note, B means the medium-radio-duty battery run; its supply voltage crossed the cutoff at six hours. No humidity run was involved.
Humidity drift report draft: compare the wet ramp against the dry control, subtract initial offset, and report baseline change rather than battery duration.
Screenshot description: battery lifetime chart for Lark, low/medium/high radio duty, with the medium run cutoff marked at six hours.
Review of the humidity draft: the wet-minus-dry comparison is useful, but add uncertainty from the chamber probe calibration.
Humidity drift report delivered with the calibration uncertainty added. Keep both enclosure logs as supporting material for this study.

events.reason: c08 identifies Run B as the battery-duty-cycle run. File the restored fragment under battery lifetime.

events.text: Humidity drift report final: compare the wet ramp against the dry control, subtract initial offset, and include chamber-probe calibration uncertainty in the baseline-change estimate.

captures.text: Birch Lane library wants a rain garden to catch roof runoff. Survey the downpipe, size the basin, then check it after the first storm.
Photo description: allotment plot 18 vegetable beds under standing water. Separate drainage job: cut a shallow side swale without routing water into neighboring plots.
Library downpipe survey: the runoff crosses the paving first. The rain-garden inlet needs a stone apron so the basin edge will not wash out.
Cello audition checklist: record the prelude and the dance in one quiet room, then choose complete takes for the submission.
Skip the membrane; roots need to cross.
Library rain-garden planting plan: sedges near the inlet, flowering plugs on the higher rim. Basin depth shown as 250 mm.
The membrane note refers to plot 18's vegetable-bed swale. Leave it unlined so crop roots can cross; the library basin uses its own specification.
Order from Flint Yard: washed stone for Birch Lane library rain-garden inlet; separate gravel bags for plot 18's swale. Invoice lines have separate site codes.
Installation clip at Birch Lane library: inlet stone apron is seated, basin is excavated to the revised depth, and the sedges are planted.
Plot 18 after rain: the new unlined side swale drains, but a low corner of the vegetable bed still holds water. Raise only that corner.
Library rain garden after its first storm: water entered over the stone apron, no rim erosion, standing water gone by the following morning.
Library rain-garden handover: keep the inlet free of leaves and recheck the sedges in six weeks. Attach the first-storm observations to the maintenance sheet.
